clue.text: Succeed in spoiling brew trust a ref!

indicators.note: a brew is something stirred up and mixed, so the following letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a cup of tea and calls for the referee's help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brew' is the anagram signal on TRUST A REF; the exclamation reads as a plea but is pure fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart a plan is to manage to wreck it, which is the same as succeeding in spoiling it.

clue.text: Depleted fuel, or a form of life on earth

indicators.note: depleted means run down or emptied, so the middle letters of the word fuel are drained away

explanation.surface: Low fuel threatens some kind of earthly existence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depleted' drains the inside of the word, leaving only its outer letters; 'or a' then sits in the clue as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The plants of a region are its vegetable life, one form of life found on earth.

clue.text: Leading cheering and taking life from the earth

parts.note: a team that is leading is up, ahead in the score
rooting means cheering on a side, as in rooting for a team

explanation.surface: A supporter is ahead and cheering while pulling plants out of the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling a plant out by the roots removes living growth from the soil.

clue.text: Break up estate to cover auction of mosaic

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cover, or wrap around, the next piece
to break up something is to smash it into pieces, so the letters of estate are rearranged

parts.note: to auction goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: Someone breaks up a property to pay for buying a mosaic at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break up' looks like dividing the estate, but it makes TESATE, which 'to cover' wraps around the sale word; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiles fitted together without gaps form a chequered pattern, the defining feature of a mosaic.

clue.text: Chief is in some confusion

indicators.note: the phrase is in tells us the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: some and any are interchangeable, as in 'have you any?'
arch means chief or principal, as in archenemy

explanation.surface: The boss is in a bit of a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawlessness with no government brings disorder and confusion.

clue.text: The heart of a German town church

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in western Germany
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church lies at the centre of a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The core or basic nature of something is its very heart.

clue.text: Money is invested in change, giving conflict

indicators.note: money that is invested is put into something, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: loose change is cash
L stands for pound, the sign for money in sterling (from the Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Investing money in loose change leads to a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash is a fight or disagreement, a kind of conflict.

clue.text: Yield to one of the top players in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the word is spoken, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: in a tennis tournament the top players are ranked as seeds

explanation.surface: A player gives way to one of the tournament's favourites in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up territory or a point is to surrender it, to yield it.

clue.text: "Home is the sailor" (poem)

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A line about the sailor coming home, presented as a poem title.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation recalls Stevenson's 'Requiem' ('Home is the sailor, home from sea'); 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling place is where one lives, one's home.

clue.text: Spooner's porridge, darling, is the price of silence

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the openings of words, so the first sounds of the two pieces trade places

parts.note: mush is soft food such as porridge
honey is a term of endearment like darling

explanation.surface: Porridge served with an endearment turns out to cost someone's silence.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSH HONEY with the initial M and H swapped gives HUSH MONEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A bribe paid to keep someone quiet is the cost of buying their silence.

clue.text: Awful rogues without class -the fiends

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the remaining letters are jumbled
without means the next piece is taken away

parts.note: U stands for upper class, the old label for posh usage

explanation.surface: Dreadful scoundrels lacking breeding are monsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops U (upper class) from ROGUES, and 'Awful' jumbles the remaining ROGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are cruel monsters of folklore, a kind of fiend.

clue.text: Hard working single couple (American) on a ship

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, puts the single couple American after the a-ship pair

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a duo is a pair or couple
US means American

explanation.surface: A diligent unmarried American pair aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Being diligent and persevering means working hard.

clue.text: Young person's state benefit in escalation

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is just the young person and the clue reads 'young person is ...'

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: an ascent is a climb or rise, an escalation
the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit paid by the state

explanation.surface: A teenager's welfare payments keep rising.
explanation.walkthrough: THE DOLE is everyday British for state unemployment pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is someone between childhood and adulthood, a young person.

clue.text: Smile at broadcast

definitions.meaning: to transmit a signal or programme

explanation.definitionFit: To grin radiantly is one sense; to transmit a radio signal is the other.

clue.text: Moriarty is one teacher to be careful of

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher
mind means watch out for, as in 'mind the step'

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes's nemesis is a schoolmaster to watch out for.
explanation.walkthrough: Professor Moriarty is the criminal genius opposing Sherlock Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Moriarty is the classic example of a criminal genius who plans everything.

clue.text: Man taken in by wage pattern

indicators.note: something taken in by another is enclosed within it

parts.note: a wage is pay
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A man's wages bring a design.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised 'Man' is the Isle of Man, not a person. PAISLEY is a swirling teardrop fabric design.
explanation.definitionFit: A Paisley is a distinctive swirling teardrop design printed on fabric.

clue.text: Figure out pagan term

indicators.note: out signals letters knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Work out what a heathen word means.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star is a geometric shape, a figure.

clue.text: Joy when kinsman is beheaded

indicators.note: beheading cuts off the head, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a kinsman is a relation

explanation.surface: Happiness at the execution of a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness and exhilaration.

clue.text: Untidy batting side taken in by neat bowling

parts.note: in cricket a batsman batting is in

indicators.note: the next piece is enclosed within the other
bowling suggests the letters rolling about into a new order

parts.note: leg side is one side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A sloppy batting team gets caught out by tidy bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides it all: 'bowling' makes EANT, and 'taken in by' sets the leg side (one half of a cricket field) within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace or polish is the opposite of stylish, hence untidy.

clue.text: Denies having to set a general up with it

indicators.note: up, in this clue, says the concealed letters are read from right to left
having means containing, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to let a senior officer sit up with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' hides the letters inside TO SET A GENeral and 'up' reads them backwards; 'with it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute or nullify a claim is to deny it.

clue.text: Timekeeper's starring in both halves

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so only the timekeeper is defined

parts.note: split the word into its two halves, star and ring; a star is a sun and to ring someone is to dial them

explanation.surface: The clock watcher is the headline act.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves of 'starring' are each replaced by a synonym: STAR = SUN, RING = DIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden device casting a shadow to show the hour is an old timekeeper.

clue.text: Place on empty ferry? Rot

parts.note: to place something is to put it
re means on or concerning

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Is it rotten to sit on a ferry with no passengers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves the first and last letters of FERRY, FY.
explanation.definitionFit: To putrefy is to decompose, to rot.

clue.text: Promises note about incomplete log book

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the note goes around the next piece

parts.note: PS is a postscript, a note at the end of a letter

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a ledger is a book of accounts, a log book

explanation.surface: A memo pledging things refers to a half-finished log.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' docks the final letter of the accounts book; 'about' then wraps the postscript around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Pledges are solemn undertakings, promises.

clue.text: Underhand and underfoot

definitions.meaning: the curved part of the sole of the foot

explanation.definitionFit: Mischievously knowing or sly is one sense; the curve under the foot is the other.

clue.text: Vice chancellor's first standard, say

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a standard is a kind of lamp, the standard lamp, a tall floor-standing light

explanation.surface: The chancellor's chief standard of misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: A standard lamp is British for a tall floor lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice (vise in US spelling) is a gripping tool, much like a clamp.

clue.text: Sweet nothing could be made with rennet

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters could be rearranged to form something else

explanation.surface: Dessert made with rennet could be just a junket.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet nothing is an affectionate word, a term of endearment.

clue.text: Chopper to sound horn in front of hospital

indicators.note: in a down clue in front of places the first piece above the second

parts.note: to toot is to sound a horn
H is the abbreviation for hospital on signs

explanation.surface: A helicopter sounds its horn outside the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' suggests a helicopter but is slang for a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Choppers is slang for teeth, which chop food.

clue.text: It's nearly 12-get some sleep!

indicators.note: nearly means almost all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a dozen is twelve

explanation.surface: Almost midnight, time to get some sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 12 as midnight, but it is the number, a dozen.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze is to nap lightly.

clue.text: Anger is no alternative to logic

indicators.note: an alternative form of the letters gives a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Anger is no substitute for logic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is thinking things through logically.

clue.text: State where I owned a small house

parts.note: I'd is short for I had, that is I owned
ho. is a short form, small, of house

explanation.surface: Where I owned a modest home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a US state in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Man coming across first pear tree

indicators.note: coming across means spanning, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man discovers his first pear tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a broadleaf tree, the one on Canada's flag.

clue.text: Survive and abandon desperate defence

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the adjective-style phrase, as in a final stand

parts.note: to last is to survive
to ditch is to abandon

explanation.surface: Endure and give up on a final stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A final stand made at the last trench is a desperate attempt at resistance.
